\section[vāḻttukaḷ]{\ta{வாழ்த்துகள்} (vāḻttukaḷ) — congratulations, good wishes}

\label{lesson:TA-C98-congrats}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for that's how it is, then the Tamil for why not.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{வாழ்த்துகள்}}
\textbf{\ta{வாழ்த்துகள்}} (\emph{vāḻttukaḷ}) — \textquotedblleft{}congratulations\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}good wishes\textquotedblright{}.

It is built on \textbf{\ta{வாழ்}}, \textquotedblleft{}to live\textquotedblright{}: to wish someone well is to wish them life.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Wishes for someone's good news.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāḻttukaḷ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāḻttukaḷ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{vāḻttukaḷ!}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for that's how it is, then the Tamil for why not, then say \emph{vāḻttukaḷ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{வாழ்த்துகள்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Congratulations, good wishes\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[aḻaippu]{\ta{அழைப்பு} (aḻaippu) — an invitation, a call}

\label{lesson:TA-C98-invitation}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for why not, then the Tamil for congratulations.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{அழைப்பு}}
\textbf{\ta{அழைப்பு}} (\emph{aḻaippu}) — \textquotedblleft{}an invitation\textquotedblright{}, and \textquotedblleft{}a call\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{அழைப்புக்கு} \ta{நன்றி}} — \textquotedblleft{}thank you for the invitation\textquotedblright{}, with the \textbf{\ta{நன்றி}} you know.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An invitation, and thanks for it.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aḻaippu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aḻaippu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{aḻaippukku naṉṟi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for why not, then the Tamil for congratulations, then say \emph{aḻaippu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{அழைப்பு} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An invitation, a call\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[paricu]{\ta{பரிசு} (paricu) — a gift, a prize}

\label{lesson:TA-C98-gift}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for congratulations, then the Tamil for an invitation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{பரிசு}}
\textbf{\ta{பரிசு}} (\emph{paricu}) — \textquotedblleft{}a gift\textquotedblright{}, and \textquotedblleft{}a prize\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{உங்களுக்கு} \ta{ஒரு} \ta{பரிசு}} — \textquotedblleft{}a gift for you\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Something to bring.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paricu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{uṅkaḷukku oru paricu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for congratulations, then the Tamil for an invitation, then say \emph{paricu} again
\end{itemize}

\section[vāruṅkaḷ]{\ta{வாருங்கள்} (vāruṅkaḷ) — please come (in)}

\label{lesson:TA-C98-comein}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for an invitation, then the Tamil for a gift.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{வாருங்கள்}}
\textbf{\ta{வாருங்கள்}} (\emph{vāruṅkaḷ}) — \textquotedblleft{}please come\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}come in\textquotedblright{}.

It is the verb \textbf{\ta{வா}}, \textquotedblleft{}come\textquotedblright{}, with the respectful \textbf{-\ta{ங்கள்}}. At the door, it is the welcome.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A welcome at the door.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāruṅkaḷ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāruṅkaḷ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{vāruṅkaḷ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for an invitation, then the Tamil for a gift, then say \emph{vāruṅkaḷ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{வாருங்கள்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please come (in)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[cāppiṭuṅkaḷ]{\ta{சாப்பிடுங்கள்} (cāppiṭuṅkaḷ) — please eat}

\label{lesson:TA-C98-eat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a gift, then the Tamil for please come in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{சாப்பிடுங்கள்}}
\textbf{\ta{சாப்பிடுங்கள்}} (\emph{cāppiṭuṅkaḷ}) — \textquotedblleft{}please eat\textquotedblright{}.

A host says it, and says it again. \textbf{\ta{சாப்பிடு}} is Tamil's everyday verb for eating.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Congratulations, an invitation, a gift, come in, please eat.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cāppiṭuṅkaḷ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cāppiṭuṅkaḷ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{cāppiṭuṅkaḷ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a gift, then the Tamil for please come in, then say \emph{cāppiṭuṅkaḷ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{சாப்பிடுங்கள்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please eat\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
